issues.description: The problem statement refers to the Genre property as an optional String named `subtype` (problem_statement.md line 20), but elsewhere in the problem text it uses the term "subgenre" (problem_statement.md line 38). The solution implementation defines the property as `subgenre: String?` (solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift lines 40-44). This naming inconsistency between the problem statement and the solution (and the ambiguous terminology inside the problem statement itself) can confuse students about the exact property name they should implement and may cause mismatches with tests or reference code.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a single, consistent name for the optional String property across all artifacts. Update the problem statement to use the same identifier as the implementation (for example, change the declaration at line 20 to `subgenre` and explicitly state the property name), or change the solution to use `subtype` if that is the intended term. Ensure template, problem description, and solution all refer to the same property name (and type: `String?`).

issues.description: The problem statement specifies that Genre should have an optional String property named `subtype` (problem_statement.md, lines 19-21). The solution implementation defines this property as `subgenre` (solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift, lines 40-44). This is an identifier naming inconsistency for the same conceptual entity (a secondary, more specific genre). Students following the problem text will implement `subtype`, while the reference solution (and possibly tests or example usage) uses `subgenre`, forcing them to map two different names to the same concept and increasing unnecessary cognitive load.
issues.suggested_fix: Use the same identifier for the secondary genre across all artifacts. Two possible fixes: (A) Update the solution to match the problem statement by renaming `subgenre` to `subtype` in the Genre struct and any references (e.g., in Client printing use `genre.subtype`). Or (B) Update the problem statement to ask for `subgenre` instead of `subtype`. Prefer making the code match the problem text (rename `subgenre` -> `subtype`) so student-facing requirements and reference implementation are consistent.
